meta.title: Persian Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 106 expressions · 47 everyday, 39 idioms, 20 proverbs · both directions
meta.desc: 106 Persian set phrases, idioms and proverbs, in three subdecks: 47 everyday phrases, 39 idioms and 20 proverbs. Both study directions come as two cards of one expression — Persian → English (see the Persian, recall the meaning) and English → Persian (see an English meaning, recall the Persian) — each with a schedule of its own. This is a companion to the five level decks, Persian A1 to C1, and not one of them: a level is a list of words, and an expression is a unit a list of words cannot see. Nothing here is taught by any of the five, so the two can be studied together without repeating an entry. The PHRASES are the expressions Wiktionary files as phrases and does not mark as idiomatic — mostly the everyday formulas a Persian speaker uses as one piece (زنده باد, مگر نه, خدا را شکر …). The IDIOMS are expressions whose meaning is not their words' (به دنیا آمدن, جان سالم به در بردن, ولش کن …), and the PROVERBS the sayings Wiktionary files as proverbs (توانا بود هر که دانا بود, هر که طاووس خواهد جور هندوستان کشد, خواستن توانستن است …). Within each subdeck the expressions come in the order of how many of Tatoeba's Persian sentences contain them, an expression ending in a verb being counted in any form of that verb; Tatoeba's Persian is small, so only 20 of the 106 are found there at all, and the rest follow in the order of how common their words are in film and television subtitles. Every expression is printed in the Persian script with Wiktionary's Iranian romanisation beneath it. Real example sentences come with 20 of the 106 expressions, three apiece for 5, with the expression picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Expressions, meanings, romanisation and the idiom and proverb labels: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Order: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR, then a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba, CC BY 2.0 FR.
